title: Task Resource API: PUT Semantics, Conditional Requests, and Status Codes

questions.prompt: A task currently has version 3 and assigneeId "u_42". A client GETs it (ETag "v3") and sends PUT /v1/projects/p1/tasks/{id} with If-Match: "v3" and the full body {"title":"Fix login","description":null,"assigneeId":null,"status":"open"}, intending to unassign the task. What is the outcome?
choices: 200 OK; the stored task has assigneeId null, version 4, and the response carries ETag "v4"
422 Unprocessable Entity, because assigneeId must be a string
200 OK; the stored task still has assigneeId "u_42", version 4, and ETag "v4"
412 Precondition Failed, because the body differs from the stored representation

questions.prompt: A client sends PUT to an existing task (status "open") without an If-Match header and with body {"status":"archived"}. What does the server respond with?
choices: 422 Unprocessable Entity listing the invalid status
409 Conflict for an invalid status transition

questions.prompt: Clients A and B both GET the same task at version 5 (ETag "v5"). A sends a valid PUT with If-Match: "v5" and it completes first; then B sends a valid PUT with If-Match: "v5". What happens to B's request?
choices: 200 OK; B's values overwrite A's (last write wins) and the version becomes 7
409 Conflict, because the status transition is checked against A's version
200 OK with version 6, since both requests were based on version 5
412 Precondition Failed; A's changes are preserved and B must re-read the task

questions.prompt: Which change best fixes the problem in the first question while keeping the endpoint consistent with REST semantics?
choices: Replace the `??` operators in the PUT handler with `||` so null values are handled
Make PUT a full replacement: require every mutable field to be present (422 otherwise) and assign the body values directly, including null; offer PATCH for partial updates
Return 204 No Content from PUT instead of 200 so clients re-fetch the task
Have clients DELETE the task and POST it again without an assigneeId
